questions.question: What is the expected major product when 2-Methylpropene ((CH3)2C=CH2) is treated with HBr?
questions.explanation: Treating 2-Methylpropene ((CH3)2C=CH2) with HBr yields 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane. Rationale: Protonation gives the stable 3° carbocation, which is captured by bromide at C2.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 3,3-Dimethyl-1-butene into 2,3-Dimethyl-2-butanol (major)?
questions.explanation: To convert 3,3-Dimethyl-1-butene into 2,3-Dimethyl-2-butanol (major), the appropriate reagent is Aqueous sulfuric acid (H3O+). Rationale: Initial 2° carbocation undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to form a more stable 3° carbocation before hydration.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when 1-Methylcyclopentene is treated with HCl (g)?
questions.explanation: Treating 1-Methylcyclopentene with HCl (g) yields 1-Chloro-1-methylcyclopentane. Rationale: Protonation occurs at C2 to form the tertiary carbocation at C1, yielding the Markovnikov chloride.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 1-Pentene into 2-Iodopentane?
questions.explanation: To convert 1-Pentene into 2-Iodopentane, the appropriate reagent is HI. Rationale: Electrophilic addition of HI follows Markovnikov's rule to produce the secondary alkyl iodide.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when 3-Methyl-1-butene is treated with HCl?

options.label: B
options.text: Both give Butane (trans releases 4 kJ/mol less heat)

questions.explanation: Treating 3-Methyl-1-butene with HCl yields 2-Chloro-2-methylbutane (major). Rationale: The 2° carbocation formed at C2 undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift from C3 to form the tertiary carbocation.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Cyclohexene into trans-1,2-Dibromocyclohexane?
questions.explanation: To convert Cyclohexene into trans-1,2-Dibromocyclohexane, the appropriate reagent is Br2 in CH2Cl2. Rationale: Backside attack of bromide on the bridged bromonium ion enforces strict anti-stereospecificity.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with H2SO4 (mild heat) to yield 2,4,4-Trimethyl-2-pentene + 2,4,4-Trimethyl-1-pentene as the major product?
questions.explanation: 2-Methylpropene (isobutene) reacts with H2SO4 (mild heat) to yield 2,4,4-Trimethyl-2-pentene + 2,4,4-Trimethyl-1-pentene. Rationale: The 3° carbocation attacks another isobutene molecule, followed by deprotonation to form branched octenes.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Ethylene is treated with Cl2 / H2O?
questions.explanation: Treating Ethylene with Cl2 / H2O yields 2-Chloroethanol + HCl. Rationale: Water acts as the nucleophile to open the chloronium ion at the adjacent carbon.
